purpose: Determine whether NOAA TBOFS gridded 3-D currents can provide a reproducible near-bed hydrodynamic exposure layer for stable Tampa seagrass transects before any hydrodynamic-seagrass association is fit.

source.name: NOAA Tampa Bay Operational Forecast System (TBOFS)
source.candidate_field: 3-D current vector components from gridded NetCDF fields

required_reports: vertical coordinate and near-bed level interpretation

network_gate.vertical_requirement: Selected current layer must have an explicit reproducible near-bed interpretation.
network_gate.failure_action: Do not use TBOFS as the primary network-wide meadow exposure layer; move to direct current/ADCP measurements or another validated near-bed product.

candidate_prospective_test_if_gate_passe.primary_exposure: node-level 90th percentile near-bed current speed, speed = sqrt(u^2 + v^2), over a frozen pre-response exposure window
candidate_prospective_test_if_gate_passe.primary_outcome: future fixed-transect focal_frequency minus baseline focal_frequency

mechanistic_prediction.baseline_frequency_x_p90_current: positive if denser established meadow state buffers hydrodynamic exposure

claim_boundary: Passing the source gate establishes physical-layer usability, not an ecological mechanism.
Do not treat surface HF-radar currents as near-bed meadow exposure.
Do not tune interpolation radius, vertical level, exposure percentile or time window against a Tampa biological outcome.
A supported prospective interaction would be consistent with meadow-state buffering of hydrodynamic exposure, not proof of causal self-facilitation.
